mappings.note: Hygiene during menstruation for comfort and to avoid infection is the good-sanitation-practices strand of LO-78.
What sanitary pads and cloth pads are for: the materials of menstrual hygiene practice.
Wrapping a used pad and binning it is safe disposal, which LO-78 covers both as sanitation and as keeping waste out of the surroundings.
The Menstrual Hygiene Scheme supplies pads to rural girls, a public programme aimed squarely at sanitation practice.
Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram is about adolescent health and peer education broadly, so it sits with the everyday-health items rather than the sanitation ones.
Exercise boosting mood as well as fitness: a habit recommended for daily life.
Being respectful and careful online is conduct towards others, the values strand. Not LO-77, because the answer is about how to treat people rather than a health practice.
Cyberbullying defined as harassing or spreading falsehoods about others online: the values outcome again, here on the harm side.
Refusing tobacco, alcohol and drugs because they are addictive and damage health is a health decision in daily life. Not LO-80, since no myth or social pressure is being confronted in the answer.
What addictive means, a strong urge that develops after first use, describes how dependence sets in. A process explained rather than a practice recommended.
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan as the campaign against substance abuse, a public health measure in the same family as the other health items.
Hormones defined as chemical messengers that regulate growth and puberty: the mechanism of the process. Not LO-69, because no particular change is being traced to them here.
Where hormones are made and how the brain signals their release: more of the same mechanism.
Assertion and reason tie the whole set of adolescent changes to hormones as their cause, which is the relate-phenomenon-to-cause outcome rather than a description of how hormones work.
Roti, dal, vegetables and curd chosen over chips and sugary drinks: diet applied to real meals.
Unscrambles menstruation, the name of the process. Vocabulary of the reproductive process, so LO-70.
Unscrambles puberty, again the name of the maturation process.
The multiple-choice version of the Shalu claim, requiring adolescence to be split into physical, emotional, behavioural and biological change: categories, so LO-67.
Explains why the belief that one can stop any time is dangerous, which is correcting a false and comforting assumption. Objectivity rather than a health tip, so LO-80.
Goitre against a developing Adam's apple: two similar bulges separated by their causes.
Picks the change seen only in boys, which requires boys and girls to be set against each other. Not LO-67, because nothing is sorted into a scheme; one distinguishing feature is chosen.
Picks the change common to both sexes, the mirror image of the boys-only item and the same comparison skill.
What healthy-lifestyle advice a poster should carry: diet, hygiene, exercise, avoiding substances, mental well-being. Content rather than design, so LO-77, unlike the make-a-poster item on LO-79.
The answer is the health risk of pregnancy before the body has matured, so the item lands on health in daily life. The social-evil framing does not change what is actually assessed.
A yoga camp on International Yoga Day is physical activity taken up as practice.
Best description of adolescence as rapid change across physical, biological, emotional and behavioural domains: the category set again.
Secondary against primary sexual characteristics, one present from birth and the other emerging at puberty: an explicit differentiation of two classes of feature.
Turning to a trusted adult when facing bullying or pressure is the cooperation and freedom-from-fear strand of LO-80.
Picks experimenting with harmful substances as the practice that does not belong in a healthy adolescence: everyday health choices.
Names adolescence as the stage between childhood and adulthood.
The ten-to-nineteen age band, the defining marker of the stage.
Names the Adam's apple from the visible bump in the throat.
Names acne, the pimple condition, from what is seen on the skin. The item on why it happens is on LO-69.
Names the secondary sexual characteristics category from its definition.
Names puberty as the stage in which the body becomes able to reproduce.
Names the menstrual cycle, the recurring process.
Names menstruation as the bleeding phase within that cycle.
The age at which menstruation ends, the closing point of the reproductive process.
Calcium named for bone growth: a nutrient for the adolescent diet.
Iron named for blood formation, the companion nutrient item.
Names a menstrual hygiene product, which belongs with the sanitation practice items rather than the diet ones.
Names cyberbullying, conduct towards others and so the values outcome.
Names addiction from the repeated urge it produces: the dependence process, matching the item that defines addictive.
Names substance abuse as continued use over time, health vocabulary for the choices this chapter urges.
Names a harmful substance to avoid, the plainest of the health-choice items.
